title: India Caps Margins on 137 Cancer Drugs, Prices to Fall Up to 70% From November 9
excerpt: The NPPA limited trade margins to 30% of MRP on 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines, including Pembrolizumab and Osimertinib, in a Gazette order dated October 17.
body:
• India's NPPA has capped trade margins at 30% of MRP on 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs, with revised prices taking effect November 9, 2026.
  • The government expects MRPs to fall by up to 70% on some medicines, depending on existing mark-ups, which averaged about 170% and reached 700% in some cases.
  • Covered drugs include Pembrolizumab, Durvalumab, Osimertinib, Bevacizumab, Denosumab and Pegfilgrastim, used across more than 20 cancer types.
  • For families supporting treatment in India: manufacturers must file revised prices within 7 days of the October 17 Gazette notification, and hospitals and retailers must charge the revised prices from November 9 — check the new MRP before paying after that date.

India will cut the prices of 137 anti-cancer medicines by up to 70% from November 9, after the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) capped trade margins on the drugs at 30% of the maximum retail price, the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers said on Saturday, according to Reuters.

How the Cap Works

The order, issued through Gazette notification S.O. 5690(E) dated October 17, 2026, uses the NPPA's extraordinary powers under Paragraph 19 of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013, according to Medical Dialogues. It covers non-scheduled formulations containing any of the 137 listed drugs, alone or in combination, at any strength or dosage form, and applies to branded and generic, domestic and imported, and patented and non-patented products alike.

https://x.com/Indian_Analyzer/status/2111657520427319673

Trade margin is the gap between what a medicine costs entering the distribution chain and what the patient finally pays. The government said market data showed an average mark-up of about 170% on non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines, with some reaching 700%. Capping that margin at 30% is what produces the expected price falls of up to 70% on the most heavily marked-up products; medicines with smaller existing margins will fall by less.

Which Medicines Are Covered

The list, recommended by an expert committee under the Directorate General of Health Services, includes immunotherapy drugs used across more than 20 types of cancer. The ministry named Pembrolizumab, Durvalumab and Osimertinib among the widely used medicines covered, along with Bevacizumab for colon, ovarian and cervical cancers, Denosumab used by breast and prostate cancer patients, and Pegfilgrastim, used to prevent neutropenia during chemotherapy.

The move builds on a 2019 exercise that capped margins on 42 anti-cancer drugs and cut prices by as much as 90%. One government statement cited potential annual patient savings of up to Rs 25 billion (about $263 million).

What Happens Next

Manufacturers must inform the NPPA of revised prices within seven days of the Gazette notification. From November 9, retailers and hospitals must charge and display the revised prices, and hospitals must publish them on their websites, IANS reported. Patients can check revised prices on the NPPA website and the Pharma Sahi Daam app. Sudarshan Jain, secretary general of the Indian Pharmaceutical Alliance, said the measures would optimise oncology prices while leaving adequate margins for channel partners, according to reports of the announcement.

For diaspora families who fund a parent's or relative's treatment in India, the practical step is timing: prescriptions filled on or after November 9 should be billed at the revised MRP for covered formulations, and the medicine's name on the NPPA list is the check to make before paying a hospital pharmacy bill.
